conditions.description: Selected work is technically stopped in the observed local persistent stock workflows. Cleanup holds maintenance and complete root and actual spawn-descendant writer ownership through fresh validation. Independent work may continue.

Related selected-thread metadata updates and dependency-reference publication, including a new fork history reference, must finish before cleanup. Acquiring a writer guard does not independently certify their completion.
The selected rollout locations and every affected database and log location use the qualified local filesystem and cooperative writer and SQLite locks.
No NFS or cross-host filesystem behavior is covered, and no offline database cutover or arbitrary operator replacement may run concurrently.
A catalogue activity label, age or a writer-lock observation alone does not certify quiescence; exact native ownership and fresh execution checks remain required.
This scoped assessment does not certify historical-body integrity, a complete Core lifecycle, generic Rust equivalence or the source and signature of an observed producer binary.
Only qualified owner, provider, attachment and Guardian representations are covered; unsupported Internal Guardian selections remain protected or refused.
This record does not establish producer binary identity, verify its own origin, prove current quiescence or authorize a cleanup operation.

The actual producer and helper use matching qualified roots for the state database, companion databases, logs and selected rollout locations. Neither this record nor the helper request independently observes that the producer uses those locations.
Ordinary cache, plugin, process and output paths do not alias selected storage locations.

Stock tests used a local scripted model provider and the observed 0.171.0 producer. Additional Guardian and attachment representations have disposable storage-fixture coverage. All clients deleting from a home must use the Keep-capable helper to enforce Keep marks.
The observed producer executable digest identifies the executable exercised. It does not attest the build provenance of a caller-provided producer.

review.scope: Selected technically stopped persistent local work from stock Codex CLI 0.171.0 with the published 0.6.0 helper on the qualified Linux x86_64 host. Stock cases cover V1 legacy parent and paginated child, V2 legacy and paginated work, and a retained paginated fork that depends on its provider. The stock producer source is unchanged from the previous 0.171.0 assessment. Compared with the 0.5.2 helper, wire 7 separately validates age policy and exact-ID ceilings. Keep is checked under the same maintenance ownership before deletion. The writer, incoming attachment and physical-provider checks, fresh SQL validation and rollout-before-state ordering are retained.

source_origin.scope: Selected technically stopped persistent local work from stock Codex CLI 0.171.0 with the published 0.6.0 helper on the qualified Linux x86_64 host. Stock cases cover V1 legacy parent and paginated child, V2 legacy and paginated work, and a retained paginated fork that depends on its provider.

witnesses.scope: Matched wire-7 helper and Keep. Disposable native storage fixtures cover qualified representation, ownership, writer and exact-effect checks.

V1 legacy parent with paginated child. With a live writer, the released helper refused without effects. After the work stopped, deletion removed only the chosen child. The retained parent and unrelated thread remained readable.

V2 paginated. With a live writer, the released helper refused without effects. After the work stopped, deletion removed only the chosen child. The retained parent and unrelated thread remained readable.

Installed CLI protected a selected child with Keep, then cleared, removed and reconciled it. Installed MCP confirmed the selected V2 paginated child and observed the original attempt after restart without redispatch. Retained rollouts kept their original bytes.
On separate V2 legacy homes, CLI, Textual and MCP each removed one selected child. Fresh stock processes read and resumed each retained parent and refused the removed child.
An installed preview retained a selected provider needed by an excluded paginated fork. Both histories stayed intact and could be read and resumed by stock Codex.
